newsitem.title: FRANCE: Britain's Goss gets French award for yacht rescue.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Goss gets French award for yacht rescue.

text.p: British yachtsman Pete Goss on Thursday received France's top award, the Legion of Honour, for abandoning a round-the-world sailing race to rescue a French rival off Australia earlier this year.

French President Jacques Chirac called Goss "a sailor who has always been living by and for the sea" as he pinned the medal with its red ribbon on his blazer in a ceremony at the Elysee presidential palace.

The winner of the Vendee Globe race, Frenchman Christophe Auguin, also received the award. Frenchwoman Catherine Chabot, the first woman to complete a non-stop unassisted round-the world sailing race, received the lesser National Merit Order.

Goss gave up any chance of winning the race by going to the rescue of stricken 25-year-old French competitor Raphael Dinelli, whose yacht had capsized in remote and heavy seas about 1,000 miles (1,600 km) south of Australia.

Chirac called the rescue "an act of bravery worthy of a very great sailor, a splendid example of solidarity and generosity". He also paid tribute to Canadian competitor Gerry Roufs who disappeared in a remote Antarctic area between New Zealand and Cape Horn.
"You don't do these things for medals, do you? It's just something that you do," Goss told reporters, admitting he was "deeply honoured and moved".

"It's not just me up here," he said, adding he was accepting the medal on behalf of Australian air force pilots who saved Dinelli's life by dropping him a life raft, and of the designers and builders of his yacht.
"There's a lot of warmth from France, It's very, very special," he said.
After rescuing Dinelli, Goss had to restart the 22,000-mile Vendee Globe race from Tasmania but was credited with the time taken up with the rescue.
He ended the race fifth out of six finishers last March and sailed into the French port Le Sables D'Olonne to a hero's welcome by 150,000 people.
"The Vendee Globe is the best thing I've ever done," he said. He added he wanted to compete against Dinelli again, perhaps in a transatlantic race in October.
